q: `display(df.summary())` shows `count = 4286` for `age` in a table of 5,000 rows. What does that tell you?
o: The table has 4,286 distinct ages
714 rows have a null `age`
summary() sampled the table
714 ages are outliers
e: The count row of `summary()` counts only non-null values. The gap to the row count is the number of nulls.

q: 27% of subscribers churned. Why does that matter before training?
o: Spark ML cannot train on imbalanced labels
It means the label column has nulls
Delta tables cannot store imbalanced data
A model that always predicts "stays" already reaches 73% accuracy, so accuracy alone is misleading
e: With an imbalanced label, look at per-class metrics and keep the class ratio when you split and sample.

q: What does `SELECT * FROM t VERSION AS OF 0` do to the table `t`?
o: Nothing: it only reads the data as it was at version 0
It rolls `t` back to version 0
It deletes versions after 0
It creates a new version 0
e: Time travel reads are read-only. To change the table back, use `RESTORE TABLE ... TO VERSION AS OF`, which writes a new version.

q: You want to retrain on exactly the same data in six months. What is the safe plan?
o: Write down the date and use `timestampAsOf` later
Nothing: Delta keeps every version forever
Record the version, and save a copy of the training snapshot because VACUUM and log retention remove old versions
Run `OPTIMIZE` so the version is kept
e: By default VACUUM removes unreferenced files older than 7 days and history is kept for 30 days. Time travel is not a long-term backup.

q: Which Data profiling type fits a growing table of model predictions?
o: Snapshot
Time series
None: profiling only works on feature tables
Inference
e: An inference profile tracks prediction drift and, when labels are available, model quality metrics.
